definition: Generating natural-language descriptions of video content, combining visual encoding with sequence decoding.
details: Generating natural-language descriptions of video content, combining visual encoding with sequence decoding.

explainer.lead: Video Captioning generates natural-language descriptions of video content. It matters because it turns visual sequences into text that machines and people can search and read.

tiers.eli5: It's like having someone watch a clip and write a sentence saying what happens in it.
tiers.practitioner: Systems pair a visual encoder over the frames with a sequence decoder that emits the description. The two-stage design is the core pitfall to watch: caption quality depends on what the encoder captures.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as generating natural-language descriptions of video content by combining visual encoding with sequence decoding. It is described at that architectural level, without specific formulas or stated benchmark limits.

explainer.example: A model encodes the frames of a short clip and the decoder outputs a one-sentence description of what happens in it.
